title: I2S Signal Reader
description: I2S carries audio on three wires. The bit clock ticks once per bit, the word select line says which channel the bits belong to (low = left, high = right), and the serial data line carries the bits themselves, most significant bit first. A bit is sampled at each rising edge of the bit clock.

learningObjectives: The learner will interpret simplified I2S waveforms by reading the value of the left-channel sample from the serial data line in 6 waveforms, with at least 5 of 6 correct.
prerequisites: I2S, bit clock, word select, serial data line, most significant bit first, signed 8-bit numbers (all defined in this chapter above the block, and in Chapter 3 for bit depth).

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Explore, then fixed-order practice items with one attempt each and immediate explained feedback
keyQuestions: Which wire tells the receiver whose sample the bits are?
Waveforms 5 and 6 are 45 and -45. How do you get one bit pattern from the other?
What would go wrong if the receiver read the bits least significant bit first?
commonMisconceptions: (1) The word select line carries audio. (2) The least significant bit is sent first. (3) Both channels are always sent in the same word.
assessmentOpportunities: Complete all six waveforms. Mastery is 5 of 6 correct on the first attempt.
